children: Container and dry cargo segments each recorded 15 per cent growth during the first half, while rail volumes declined 13 per cent

Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (Apsez) handled 46 million metric tonnes (MMT) of cargo in September, registering an 11 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase. Container volumes led the growth, rising 15 per cent YoY during the month.

The September performance took Apsez’s total cargo handling during the first half of FY27 to 280 MMT, marking a 15 per cent increase compared with the corresponding period last year. Container and dry cargo volumes both grew 15 per cent YoY during the six-month period.

The growth in H1 FY27 was supported by higher volumes across key cargo categories, with containers and dry cargo recording similar growth rates. The performance comes as Apsez continues to expand its integrated network spanning ports, logistics and marine services.

Apsez operates 19 ports and terminals, including 15 in India and four international facilities across Australia, Colombo, Israel and Tanzania. Its logistics network connects ports with hinterland markets through rail, road, warehouses and multimodal infrastructure.

The company’s logistics business handled 62,302 twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) through rail in September, registering a 3 per cent YoY increase. However, the monthly improvement has not reversed the decline recorded during the first half of FY27.

Rail volumes stood at 312,763 TEUs during H1 FY27, down 13 per cent from the year-ago period. The contrasting monthly and half-year trends point to a weaker rail performance during the earlier part of the financial year.

Apsez reported a 10.2 per cent YoY increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 3,649.5 crore in Q1 FY27, compared with Rs 3,310.6 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue from operations rose 18.6 per cent to Rs 10,820.8 crore, while consolidated EBITDA increased 19 per cent to Rs 6,541 crore.

International ports were a key contributor to the quarterly performance, with revenue rising 80 per cent YoY to Rs 1,747 crore. EBITDA from international ports increased 256 per cent to Rs 730 crore, supported by operations in Australia and Colombo.

Domestic ports revenue increased 12 per cent YoY to Rs 6,964 crore, while marine revenue rose 67 per cent to Rs 901 crore. The company has retained its FY27 guidance of Rs 43,000-45,000 crore in revenue and Rs 25,000-26,000 crore in Ebitda.
